text:
Pontus Holmberg had 22 points in 70 games for Tampa Bay last season. He has 13 in 20 this year, with 6 goals, including two in the third period of a comeback try in Winnipeg on Nov. 8. For a former sixth-round pick who arrived from Toronto as a depth forward, that is a real jump.

Some of it is a hot stick. He is scoring on 18.8% of his shots, above the top of the range our numbers expect for him, and his points per 60 minutes sit well above it too. He has gone three games without a point and two without a shot, which is what a cooling stretch looks like.

What holds up is the rest of his game. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season, and he drew more penalties than he took. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man who lives off the rush: 52% of his shots came in transition. If the goals slow down, that is the part of his game we'd watch.
headline: Pontus Holmberg's scoring pace has outrun his chances
